parsed.explanation: Trans identity is not criminalised and same-sex conduct is long lawful, with no documented organised police targeting of visitors. The dominant exposure is the nationally enacted 2025 birth-sex public-restroom restriction, including for trans youth, framed as protection against harassment risks — a tier-1 universal-exposure measure with no documented working remedy for visitors. No hate-crime or anti-discrimination protection is in force, public institutions are reported to contribute to discrimination, and a 2024 report says hate crimes rose with trans women most affected, but magnitude versus background violence is undocumented and cannot be inferred. Mitigating recourse exists but is delayed and partial: a 2025 court ruling against an anti-equality decree, a venue-staff conviction, and, after nearly 20 years, 17-year sentences for police torture/sexual abuse. This places the jurisdiction in elevated risk, below 0.45-type cases with effective facility access.
